- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from recent high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–3% per sentiment shift >0.2.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends in 30-day horizon; add 1–3% upward bias if recent 7-day average is below 30-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.2–0.4), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- If true outcome is consistently below 30-day forecast, model exhibits “overconfident” bias; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 30d horizon.
